title: Geometric Rigidity via Almost-Harmonic Twisted Spinors
summary: We establish sharp scalar-curvature bounds and rigidity consequences of Gromov's exact-lift two-form method. Let $(M^n,g)$, $n\geq 4$ even, be a closed spin Riemannian manifold carrying a homologically $\hat{A}$-non-singular closed two-form $ω$ whose lift to the universal cover $X$ is exact. Then $$\inf_M\scal_g\leq -\frac{4n}{n-1}λ_0(X).$$ Equality forces $g$ to be Einstein; if $λ_0(X)>0$, then $X$ is real hyperbolic, while if $λ_0(X)=0$ and $\int_Mω^{n/2}\neq 0$, then $g$ is flat. The proof combines Gromov's twisted $L^2$-index with a conformal interpretation of the refined Kato equality…
